findings.title: deleteCache mutation never invalidates connectedCalendars, so stale cache status stays on screen
findings.body: The `deleteCache` mutation only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess` prop; unlike the `disconnectMutation` right below it, it does not call `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()`. `onSuccess`/`onChanged` is optional and is not guaranteed to refetch (several callers of `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper` don't pass it). After a successful deletion the dropdown continues to show 'Cache Status / Last updated: …' and a 'Delete cached data' item for cache rows that no longer exist, until the query happens to refetch. Add an `onSettled` that invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` as is done for the disconnect mutation.

findings.title: Access-denied/not-found case throws a plain Error, surfaced as HTTP 500
findings.body: When the credential does not exist or belongs to another user the handler throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. tRPC maps non-`TRPCError` exceptions to `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` (500) and logs them as server faults, so a user-caused condition (wrong/foreign credentialId) is reported as an outage and the client cannot distinguish it from a real failure. Throw `new TRPCError({ code: "NOT_FOUND" })` (or `FORBIDDEN`) instead, consistent with the other handlers in this router.

findings.title: Cache status ignores expiresAt, so expired cache rows are reported as live cache
findings.body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groups all `CalendarCache` rows by credentialId with no `expiresAt >= now()` filter, while `getCachedAvailability` only ever serves rows with `expiresAt >= now()`. Expired rows that have not been cleaned up will therefore make the UI show 'Cache Status / Last updated …' and offer deletion for cache that is never used for availability. Filter on `expiresAt: { gte: new Date() }` so the displayed status matches what is actually served.

findings.title: Backfilling updatedAt with NOW() makes every legacy cache row look freshly refreshed
findings.body: The migration sets `updatedAt = NOW()` for all existing `CalendarCache` rows. Since this column is now surfaced to users as 'Last updated: {{timestamp}}', every pre-existing (possibly weeks-old) cache entry will display the migration time as its last refresh, which is misleading for the very purpose of this feature (diagnosing stale cache). A better backfill is derivable from existing data: rows are always written with `expiresAt = now + 30 days` (`CACHING_TIME`), so `UPDATE "CalendarCache" SET "updatedAt" = "expiresAt" - INTERVAL '30 days'` after adding the column gives an accurate value. Also, the header comment ('without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty') is stale since a default was added.

findings.title: Extra SelectedCalendar.updateMany write on every cache refresh for data nothing reads
findings.body: `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` now issues `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` to bump `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` for every row under the credential. This runs on every Google webhook notification and cron refresh, adding a write touching N rows per credential, yet `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` is not consumed anywhere (the UI uses `CalendarCache.updatedAt`, and the PR description itself questions whether this should be kept). It also overwrites `updatedAt` semantics for SelectedCalendar (which previously tracked configuration changes) with 'cache refreshed'. Remove it, or make it serve a concrete purpose.

findings.title: UserWithCalendars now requires updatedAt and googleChannelId that nothing in this module uses
findings.body: `UserWithCalendars.allSelectedCalendars`/`userLevelSelectedCalendars` now require `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` on every selected calendar, but no code in `getConnectedDestinationCalendars.ts` (or the handler consuming it) reads these fields. This type is exported and re-exported through `@calcom/platform-libraries` (`getConnectedDestinationCalendars`), so any external caller that builds the user from a narrower `select` (e.g. only `externalId/integration/eventTypeId`) now fails type-checking for no functional benefit. The only reason the trpc path compiles is the matching change in `user.ts` `findUnlockedUserForSession`. Revert the type widening (and the extra `select` fields) unless the fields are actually used.

findings.title: ENV_FILE is resolved relative to the caller's CWD, writing GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL to the wrong .env
findings.body: `ENV_FILE="../.env"` is relative to the working directory, not to the script's location. The script lives in `scripts/`, so running it the usual way from the repo root (`./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` or `bash scripts/...`) resolves to the directory *above* the repository, where the script will create a stray `.env` and report success while the real `.env` is untouched. Resolve the path relative to the script, e.g. `ENV_FILE="$(dirname "$0")/../.env"`.

findings.title: sed -i '' is BSD/macOS-only and fails on GNU sed
findings.body: `sed -i '' -E ...` is the macOS/BSD form; GNU sed treats `''` as the sed script and `-E` and the real expression as filenames, failing with 'can't read ...'. Contributors on Linux will get an error instead of an updated `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL`. Use a portable approach (e.g. write to a temp file and `mv`, or detect the platform). Also note `cleanup` always `exit 0`, so the rate-limit and 'Failed to extract URL' failure paths return success.

findings.title: dev:cron switched to `npx tsx` but tsx is not a declared dependency
findings.body: The `dev:cron` script now runs `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`, yet `tsx` is not listed in `dependencies`/`devDependencies` (only `ts-node` is). `npx` will attempt to download an unpinned latest `tsx` at run time (prompting interactively, and failing offline or under `npm_config_yes=false`), which makes the script non-reproducible. Either add `tsx` as a devDependency and call it via `yarn tsx`/`tsx`, or keep `ts-node`. This change is also unrelated to the calendar-cache feature.

findings.title: Cache timestamp is formatted with a hard-coded en-US locale
findings.body: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", …)` ignores the user's locale and time format even though the surrounding string is translated via `useLocale`. Non-US users will see `7/15/25, 4:06 PM` style output regardless of their language/12h-24h preference. Use the locale from `useLocale()` (e.g. `i18n.language`) or the existing dayjs/`formatTime` helpers that respect the user's `timeFormat`.

findings.title: Cache status query bypasses the calendar-cache feature flag and runs unconditionally
findings.body: The handler instantiates `CalendarCacheRepository` directly instead of going through `CalendarCache.init()`/`CalendarCache.initFromCredentialId`, which returns the mock repository when the `calendar-cache` feature is disabled. As a result every `connectedCalendars` call (a hot query on the installed-apps page, event-type settings and onboarding) now performs an extra `groupBy` on `CalendarCache` even for deployments/teams with caching disabled, where the result is always empty. Route through the feature-flag-aware factory, or at least skip the query when `credentialIds` is empty.

findings.title: No tests for new deleteCache endpoint or dropdown, and the replaced disconnect control has no test id
findings.body: The PR adds a new authenticated tRPC mutation (`deleteCache`) with an ownership check, a new repository method, and replaces the `DisconnectIntegration` trash button with a dropdown on the connected-calendars list, but adds no unit or e2e tests. The ownership check in `deleteCacheHandler` (must not delete another user's cache) is exactly the kind of authorization logic that should have a test, and the new trigger `Button` has no `data-testid`, so existing Playwright flows that disconnect a calendar from this list can no longer target the control reliably. Add a handler test for the foreign-credential case and a test id on the dropdown trigger/items.
